label: i74-nodestructure-tmp-misalignment
expect: does $TMP's nodestructure response pair each SEU_ADT_REPOSITORY_OBJ_NODE's DESCRIPTION with its own OBJECT_NAME, given it contains a DEVC/K sub-package row?
note: Confirms the issue #74 defect directly on the wire: node 1 is the sub-package $ABAPSMITH_FLUID_API (DEVC/K), whose own <DESCRIPTION/> is empty on this node as usual, but its REAL description ('abapsmith fluid API generated objects') is not lost — it resurfaces on node 5 (CLAS/OC ZCL_I75_PROBE), four rows later. From node 5 onward every DESCRIPTION belongs to the PREVIOUS object, not its own: node 7 (CLAS/OC ZTESTAI) carries 'Class ZCL_TMP_COUNT_SFLIGHT' (node 6's own description), node 8 (INTF/OI ZIF_APACK_MANIFEST) carries 'test ai' (ZTESTAI's own description), node 12 (CHKV/TYP ZABAP_CLOUD_DEVELOPMENT) carries 'tmp', and node 13 (NROB/NRO BIM0000002) finally carries ZABAP_CLOUD_DEVELOPMENT's own real description ('Default ATC variant for ABAP Cloud Development'). The shift persists for the rest of the 389-row list; the true description of the very last object (Z_REF_PO_APPR) falls off the end and is never emitted anywhere. This is a server-side defect in the response payload itself, reproduced here with a raw curl POST and a regex over the raw XML bytes — not a parser artifact. See INDEX.md for the full ground-truth pairing table (five objects individually re-read at their own ADT resource: ZTESTAI, ZIF_APACK_MANIFEST, ZABAP_CLOUD_DEVELOPMENT, ZAPI_TRAVEL_U_V2_0001, $ABAPSMITH_FLUID_API). Paired with capture 885 (informationsystem/search for the same package), which resolves all 389 objects to their correct descriptions by (type, name) key instead of wire position.
